generalizedRange: Lord Howe Island group, Tasman Sea, off eastern Australia
hook: Gone by 1935. In 2001, three turned up on one shrub on a sea stack.

story.text: Islanders called it the tree lobster: a glossy black, hand-length stick insect once so common it was used as fishing bait.
Wingless and nocturnal, it rests by day in tree hollows — in 1916 an entomologist counted 68 in one.
In 1918 the supply ship Makambo ran aground, ship rats came ashore, and the last was seen on the island in 1920.
By 1935 it was recorded as very rare, if not already extinct.
In 2001 a night survey of Balls Pyramid, a sea stack 23 km away, found two adults and one nymph on a few Melaleuca shrubs.
The whole known wild population fed on six shrubs in a patch 30 metres by 6.
On Valentine's night 2003 two pairs were carried to the mainland; at Melbourne Zoo, Eve laid 248 eggs and the first nymph hatched that September.
The program has since raised 19 generations, holds 700–800 insects, and shares eggs with zoos in San Diego, Bristol, Toronto and Prague.
Between May and December 2019 the Lord Howe Island Board baited the island for rats and mice; by July 2023 none had been found for over two years.
To witness the Lord Howe Island stick insect is to keep a door open — back to the island forest it was lost from, now without rats.

stats.size: Females to 15 cm · about 25 g — hand-length
stats.diet: Melaleuca howeana leaves · eaten at night
stats.populationEstimate: Fewer than 50 mature in the wild
stats.populationAsOf: 2012 · per NSW Threatened Species Scientific Committee

reproduction.text: A female lays clutches of nine or ten eggs, up to 300 in her life, each taking six to nine months to hatch — and unfertilised eggs can hatch too, all of them female.

insight.text: Hatchlings emerge bright green and darken with every moult to glossy black — and by day the young pile together in living clusters inside hollow logs.

programs.title: Melbourne Zoo breeding program
programs.summary: Breeds the species at Melbourne Zoo from the two pairs collected on Balls Pyramid in 2003, shares eggs with partner zoos overseas, and plans to release free-ranging insects on Lord Howe Island once it stays rat-free.

programs.title: Rodent Eradication Project
programs.summary: Baited Lord Howe Island for ship rats and house mice between May and December 2019, then ran a July 2023 checkpoint search with 140 tracking tunnels, 32 trail cameras and detection dogs that found none.
